description: Salesforce is a cloud-based customer relationship management (CRM) platform that enables organizations to manage customer data, sales, support cases, service workflows, analytics, and automation through programmatic access to org data and metadata.
api_breadth: Comprehensive API coverage across sObjects (Accounts, Contacts, Cases, etc.), metadata description, SOQL querying, Composite APIs, Bulk data batch operations, Invocable Actions, Analytics (Reports and Dashboards), Chatter/Connect API, and single-endpoint GraphQL operations. Limitations include org-level API call limits and dependency on enabled features/packages or user permissions.
existing_mcp: Official and third-party MCP servers exist. Salesforce provides official hosted MCP servers (GA for Enterprise Edition and above) and the official salesforcecli/mcp repository. Third-party MCP implementations include @aiondadotcom/mcp-salesforce and salesforce-docs-mcp.
buildability: Highly practical. Salesforce has extensive public API documentation, standardized OAuth 2.0 authentication flows (Client Credentials, Authorization Code, JWT, etc.), wide sObject and metadata API breadth, and mature official and community MCP tools.
main_blocker: API access requires supported Salesforce editions (such as Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, or Developer Edition) with API permissions enabled, as well as configuration of Connected Apps or External Client Apps to manage OAuth credentials.

description: HubSpot is a comprehensive CRM, marketing, sales, and service platform designed to help businesses manage customer relationships, inbound marketing, sales pipelines, and customer service operations.
api_breadth: HubSpot exposes robust REST and GraphQL APIs covering core CRM objects (contacts, companies, deals, tickets), engagements, marketing, CMS, conversations, and settings. Operations include complete CRUD capabilities, associations, and batch endpoints, with date-based versioning schemes.
existing_mcp: HubSpot publishes official MCP servers (including a hosted server at mcp.hubspot.com and a local developer MCP server) offering read and write access to CRM objects.
buildability: Extremely practical to build an integration due to high-quality documentation, comprehensive official SDKs, public self-serve access, standard authentication mechanisms, and native official MCP support.
main_blocker: Rate limits (such as burst limits ranging from 110 to 190 requests per 10 seconds) and the need to handle scheduled platform API deprecations/version migrations.

description: Pipedrive is a web-based Sales CRM and pipeline management tool designed to help sales teams plan their selling processes and manage deals, contacts, leads, and activities.
api_breadth: Comprehensive REST API coverage across deals, contacts, organizations, leads, activities, products, pipelines, stages, notes, and files via v1 and v2 active versions. Lacks coverage for upstream intelligence data like company tech stacks or buying intent.
existing_mcp: Both official and third-party MCP servers exist. Pipedrive runs its own official hosted MCP server, while third-party implementations (such as community packages on GitHub and directories) also exist.
buildability: High. The application features mature REST endpoints, published OpenAPI 3 specs, official SDKs, OAuth 2.0 support, and developer sandbox accounts.

description: Attio is a modern, flexible, and data-driven customer relationship management (CRM) platform that allows revenue teams to build a custom CRM around their unique data model with customizable objects, attributes, lists, and workflows.
api_breadth: The REST API provides comprehensive CRUD access to core objects and resources, including records, lists, objects, attributes, tasks, notes, threads, comments, and webhooks. Published whole-API limits are 100 requests per second for reads and 25 requests per second for writes, with additional complexity-based score limits on list queries.
existing_mcp: Attio provides an official hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server located at mcp.attio.com/mcp. There are also third-party community implementations available, such as kesslerio/attio-mcp-server on GitHub.
buildability: High buildability due to comprehensive public REST documentation, open interactive explorers, clear OpenAPI specifications, multi-language SDK support, and flexible authentication methods.
main_blocker: Score-based query limits on list queries that grow more expensive as the workspace scales, alongside uniqueness conflicts when configuring webhook subscriptions.

description: Twenty is an open-source, self-hostable CRM and platform that provides developer-friendly tools, object declaration, server-side functions, and workspace-generated schema-per-tenant APIs.
api_breadth: Core API (/rest/ and /graphql/) provides CRUD operations on records such as People, Companies, Opportunities, and custom objects. Metadata API (/rest/metadata/ and /metadata/) provides schema management to create, modify, or delete objects, fields, and relations. Rate limits are set to 100 requests per minute and 60 records per batch call.
existing_mcp: Third-party MCP server implementation exists (such as jezweb/twenty-mcp), but no official first-party MCP server was found.
buildability: Highly buildable. Twenty provides dynamic workspace-specific REST and GraphQL APIs generated directly from the schema, robust batch operation support, and comprehensive developer tooling, though developers must account for workspace-specific endpoints and rate limits.

description: Podio is a flexible work management and collaboration platform that lets teams build custom apps, workspaces, and workflows for project management, CRM, and internal operations.
api_breadth: The Podio API offers complete programmable access to all Podio functionality including applications, items, tasks, workspaces, users, files, comments, and webhooks.
existing_mcp: An official MCP server exists provided directly by Progress Software at https://mcp.podio.com in beta, and a third-party implementation exists via Activepieces.
buildability: Highly practical. The platform provides comprehensive REST documentation, multiple official client libraries, webhooks, and explicit OAuth 2.0 authentication flows.

description: DealCloud is a flexible CRM and deal management platform used by financial services, investment banking, and private equity industries to track relationships, companies, contacts, and deals.
api_breadth: The REST APIs cover Authentication, User Management, Schema metadata, Data manipulation via Cells and Rows, Backups, and Publications. There are also GraphQL capabilities exposed via the platform and MCP servers.
existing_mcp: An official MCP server is provided out-of-the-box by DealCloud (Intapp Celeste).
buildability: Building a custom integration is straightforward given the detailed REST and GraphQL API documentation, interactive Swagger specifications, and native MCP support, provided the user has proper enterprise licensing and admin permissions enabled.
main_blocker: Requires a specific enterprise subscription tier, appropriate administrative privileges, and explicit capability toggling within user management.

description: Zendesk is a cloud-based customer service software and support ticketing system designed to help businesses manage customer support workflows, track tickets, manage user and organization data, and run multi-channel help centers and messaging.
api_breadth: Zendesk offers comprehensive API coverage organized across product capabilities including Ticketing, Help Center, AI Agents, Messaging, Voice (Talk), Sales CRM, and Custom Data. Key resources include tickets, users, organizations, articles, and macros, supporting operations such as CRUD, search, and workflow automation. Note that Support API tokens are being phased out and replaced by OAuth.
existing_mcp: Third-party MCP server exists (e.g., Zendesk MCP Server by SShadowS).
buildability: Practical to build. Zendesk has extensive, well-documented REST APIs and OAuth support, though developers must migrate away from deprecated API tokens. Third-party MCP implementations also exist to accelerate development.
main_blocker: Deprecation and phase-out of legacy Support API tokens requiring OAuth implementation.
